ledger.x: 1805: Muhammad Ali becomes wali of Egypt.
1805: Muhammad Ali's Egypt is the Sultan's vassal from the start.
1811: the Ottoman-Egyptian army lands in Arabia against the Emirate of Diriyah.
1818: Diriyah falls to Ibrahim Pasha.
1820: Muhammad Ali's army enters the Sudan.
1821: Muhammad Ali is made governor of Crete.
14 June 1821: Sennar falls.
19 August 1821: Kordofan falls.
March 1825: Ibrahim lands in the Morea.
ledger.cpn: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

ledger.x: August 1828: Egypt agrees to recall Ibrahim.
ledger.cpn: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

ledger.x: 1831: Ibrahim Pasha invades Syria.
1832: Acre falls and Syria is occupied.
1833: Egypt takes the Tihama.
1833: the Convention of Kutahya turns the occupation of Syria into a cession.
May 1833: the occupation of Crete becomes a grant.
1833: the Ottomans cede Syria to Egypt.
1833: the First Egyptian-Ottoman War ends with the Convention of Kutahya after Russian intervention ('Egyptian victory').
1838: Faisal bin Turki is defeated and Najd comes under Egyptian arms.
1839: the second Egyptian-Ottoman War.
1840: Cliopatria adds Hasa to the Egyptian shape.
1840: the Egyptians lose Syria.

1840: Muhammad Ali renounces Crete and the Hejaz in the Convention of Alexandria (27 November 1840): 'Egyptian retrocession of Syria, Crete, and the Hejaz to the Ottoman Empire'; the page gives no end date for Egyptian control of the Hejaz itself.

1840: the war ends on 27 November 1840, when Muhammad Ali 'finally accepted the terms of the Convention' (the Convention of Alexandria); an Ottoman victory, with hereditary rule of Egypt and the Sudan kept and an army of 18,000 men.
27 November 1840 (Convention of Alexandria): the end of the Egyptian hold on the Tihama is bridged.
1841: the Egyptian hold on Najd and Hasa ends (bridged; moved from 1842 after review).
1865: bookkeeping end of this dossier's vassal span, not an end of the relation.
1865: the pasha's Egypt continues as the Khedivate.

wars.name: Ottoman-Wahhabi War
wars.outcome: Destruction of the Emirate of Diriyah; the Hejaz returned to Ottoman rule, with Egyptian armies as the Sultan's agent.

wars.name: Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan
wars.outcome: Egypt takes Nubia (July 1820), Sennar and the Gezira from the Funj (14 June 1821) and Kordofan from Darfur (19 August 1821) and builds the Sudan province.

wars.name: Egyptian intervention in the Greek War of Independence
wars.outcome: No border change: Egypt held land for the Sultan and kept none.

wars.name: Egyptian-Ottoman War (1831-1833)
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory: the Ottomans cede Syria to Egypt by the Convention of Kutahya (May 1833).

wars.name: Egyptian-Ottoman War (1839-1841)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory with British naval support: Egypt gives up Syria, Crete, Adana and the Hejaz and keeps hereditary rule of Egypt and the Sudan (27 November 1840; firman of 13 February 1841).

certainty.note: Egypt's own edge is the desert; the Hejaz, Sudan and Syrian lines were army zones, not surveyed frontiers.

The firman of 13 February 1841 names the extent in words (Egypt, 'the Sinai peninsula and certain places on the Arabian side of the Red Sea, and to the Sudan'); no survey line, and the Sudan's southern and western limits stay open.
